SORENSON ENGINEERING / CASE STUDY 07

Manufacturing Reel Redesign

Redesign a discontinued reel around manufacturing, assembly, and heat-treatment handling requirements.

Project type
Internship project
Role
Engineering Intern / Stamping
Timeline
Jun–Sep 2024
Disciplines
Reverse engineering · Prototyping · Drawings
Status
Design & prototyping
01 Problem02 Requirements03 Concepts04 Engineering Analysis05 Design06 Build / Test07 Results08 What I Learned
01

Problem

A supplier discontinuation created the need to redesign a manufacturing reel. Replacing the geometry alone was not enough: the reel needed to work with assembly, handling, and heat-treatment operations.

I reverse-engineered the existing system and developed updated flanges, a hub, and a clip arrangement with the production process in mind.

02

Requirements

RequirementEngineering definition
ReplacementAddress the discontinued supplier component.
AssemblyReconsider the use of permanent bolts.
HandlingSupport stackability through heat treatment.
ManufacturabilityApply design-for-manufacturing considerations to the component set.
DocumentationProduce engineering drawings for the revised design.
03

Concepts

ITERATION / 01

Understand the existing assembly

Reverse-engineer the reel and identify the interfaces that are necessary to preserve.

ITERATION / 02

Revise the component relationships

Develop flange, hub, and clip concepts, including dimples and stackability features, to improve assembly practicality.

04

Engineering Analysis

The work focused on geometry, interfaces, manufacturing feasibility, and assembly sequence. The reel had to be considered within the process that used it.

Prototypes allowed the design to be examined physically before relying on the drawing package. No FEA result or quantified production improvement is claimed for this project.

05

Design

The redesigned reel included flanges, a hub, and a clip, with dimples and stackability considered as part of the component geometry.

Replacing permanent bolts required attention to how the parts would locate, connect, and be handled. The drawing package translated those decisions into a manufacturing definition.

06

Build / Test

I used Carbon 3D-printed prototypes to support physical evaluation of the redesigned components and their assembly.

The project produced more than eight engineering drawings. Original supplier and company drawings are not reproduced on this site.

07

Results

The work connected reverse engineering with a revised component architecture, physical prototypes, and a documented design package.

8+engineering drawings
3core component types
3Dprinted prototypes
08

What I Learned

A replacement part is part of a process. Designing around assembly and heat-treatment handling helped me see manufacturability as an input from the beginning, not a check at the end.
